title: Application for Ad-Interim Ex-Parte Temporary Injunction under Order XXXIX Rules 1 & 2 read with Section 151 CPC, 1908
whenToUse: Use when seeking urgent interlocutory protection to prevent alienation, demolition, waste, damage, or third-party creation over immovable property pending disposal of suit.
variantComparisonNote: Interlocutory injunction application under Order XXXIX CPC accompanying the main plaint. Distinct from final decree of permanent injunction.
youWillNeed: Title deeds, sale deed / conveyance, revenue records (Jamabandi/Khatauni), site photographs, electricity bills proving possession.
legalBasis: Order XXXIX Rules 1 & 2 read with Section 151 Code of Civil Procedure, 1908; Specific Relief Act, 1963; Gujarat Bottling Co. Ltd. v. Coca Cola Co. (1995).
mandatoryStatutoryIngredients: Establishment of a strong prima facie case in favor of the applicant
Demonstration that balance of convenience tilts heavily in applicant's favor
Proof of imminent threat of irreparable injury not compensable by damages
Urgent grounds dispensing with prior notice under Order XXXIX Rule 3 CPC

aiBlocks.title: Possession, Title & Imminent Threat
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Narrate Plaintiff's lawful ownership and settled possession of {{FACT:property_description}}, and Defendant's overt threats of dispossession, demolition, or third-party sale.

aiBlocks.title: Tripartite Injunction Benchmark Principles
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Establish strong prima facie case, balance of convenience, and irreparable injury under Gujarat Bottling principles, justifying ex-parte ad-interim relief under Order XXXIX Rule 3.

aiBlocks.title: Prayer for Ad-Interim Temporary Injunction
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Draft explicit prayer restraining {{FACT:respondent_defendant}}, servants, and agents from alienating, creating encumbrances, or disturbing peaceful possession of {{FACT:property_description}}.
